description: Canonical registry of callable Cloud Function names. Names use the domain.action convention per docs/api-guidelines.md; this file is the single source of truth for function names across iOS, Android, backend, and admin. Every callable verifies authentication context and, in production, enforces App Check — EXCEPT explicitly-documented pre-authentication endpoints (currently only diagnostics.submitReport) which are intentionally non-enforcing because they must work before the client can mint an App Check token; see each function's appCheck field and description. All callables return error codes from contracts/errors/errors.json. The status field tracks migration progress (planned vs implemented).

accessLevels.public: No authentication required. Reserved for telemetry that must work before sign-in (diagnostics.submitReport). App Check is non-enforcing on this path so a device that cannot yet attest (the exact failure it surfaces) can still report; a valid token is still verified best-effort. This is the ONLY callable that opts out of App Check enforcement (see submitReport.ts + appcheck-guard.test.ts).
accessLevels.signedIn: Any signed-in user, including suspended — reserved for cleanup paths that must work under suspension (e.g. push token unregistration).
accessLevels.member: Requires active member_monthly entitlement; suspension always overrides entitlement.
accessLevels.admin: Requires admin or owner role; does not require member subscription.

functions.name: auth.completeOnboarding
functions.description: Marks onboarding complete for the calling user; backend writes onboardingCompletedAt and consent timestamps. Deployed via grouped export as auth-completeOnboarding (functions/src/auth/completeOnboarding.ts).

functions.name: auth.recordLogin
functions.description: Stamps userLifecycle/{uid}.lastLoginAt = serverTimestamp() on each successful sign-in (trusted server write via the Admin SDK; userLifecycle/{uid} is a backend-only side collection — owner+admin read, all client writes denied by rules — so clients can never set it, and the account's activity is not exposed on the public users/{uid} profile). The Firestore field — not Firebase Auth's non-queryable lastSignInTime — is the queryable, admin-displayable last-activity source consumed by the scheduled account-cleanupInactive sweep. Active-actor gated (requireActiveActor): ANY authenticated, non-suspended, non-deleted account records lastLoginAt — non-members included — so an actively signing-in account is never wrongly treated as inactive; only accounts that have never signed in lack a lastLoginAt and are covered by the sweep's lastLoginAt ?? createdAt fallback. Idempotent (a repeat call refreshes the timestamp); the Android client calls it best-effort after auth completes. Deployed via grouped export as auth-recordLogin (functions/src/auth/recordLogin.ts).

functions.name: subscription.verify
functions.description: Receipt-verification entry point (authenticated). FAILS CLOSED with failed-precondition until config/subscriptionProviders.{apple|google}.enabled is set with real store credentials (end-of-MVP console setup; the legacy endpoint was itself a placeholder) - no code path grants entitlement from an unverified receipt. Raw purchase tokens are hashed (SHA-256) immediately and never stored, logged, or returned. Deployed via grouped export as subscription-verify (functions/src/subscription/verify.ts).

functions.name: live.startSession
functions.description: Starts (or RESTARTS with a fresh id/expiry) the caller's live location session with a chosen duration (1h|2h|4h). Member-only; gated by the liveLocation flag. Session state lives at RTDB liveLocation/{uid}/session - backend-only writes; owner-only read. Deployed via grouped export as live-startSession (functions/src/live/session.ts).

functions.name: live.updatePosition
functions.description: Writes the caller's latest position to RTDB liveLocation/{uid}/latest (lean marker node with denormalized displayName and session expiry). Requires an ACTIVE unexpired session; enforces the contract's 60-second staleness threshold. Markers are readable by non-suspended activeMember claims only. Deployed via grouped export as live-updatePosition (functions/src/live/session.ts).

functions.name: live.stopSession
functions.description: Stops the caller's session (status stopped, stopReason) and removes the latest marker immediately. Deployed via grouped export as live-stopSession (functions/src/live/session.ts).

functions.name: live.hideMeNow
functions.description: Immediately stops the caller's session (reason hide_me_now) and removes the latest marker. signedIn access: works while SUSPENDED — removing your own position is a privacy action that must always be available. Deployed via grouped export as live-hideMeNow (functions/src/live/session.ts).

functions.name: drives.save
functions.description: Saves a completed drive: computes distanceMeters/durationSeconds/averageSpeed server-side from the submitted route points (implausible GPS jumps filtered), writes rides/{rideId}, and returns the canonical member-gated Cloud Storage paths (rideRoutes/{uid}/{rideId}/) for the client route/preview upload. Idempotent per sourceSessionId. No top-speed is ever stored. Deployed via grouped export as drives-save (functions/src/drives/saveDrive.ts).

functions.name: drives.delete
functions.description: Deletes an owned drive: removes the rideRoutes/{uid}/{rideId}/ Cloud Storage files first, then the rides/{rideId} document. Available to any active owner — membership not required (legacy parity: free users can delete drives saved during a previous membership). Deployed via grouped export as drives-delete (functions/src/drives/deleteDrive.ts).

functions.name: blocking.block
functions.description: Blocks a target user for the caller. Directional and idempotent: re-blocking keeps the original createdAt; self-blocking is invalid-argument; blocking a missing/deleted user is not-found (never permission-denied, so deletion can't be probed). Writes userBlocks/{callerUid}/blocked/{targetUid} with the denormalized displayName. Returns the block summary plus shouldRefreshMarkers. Ports services/api/src/lib/blocking-service.ts. Deployed via grouped export as blocking-block (functions/src/blocking/manageBlocks.ts).

functions.name: blocking.unblock
functions.description: Removes the caller's block against a target user. Idempotent: unblocking a non-existent block returns { unblocked: false } rather than erroring; self is always { unblocked: false }. Deletes userBlocks/{callerUid}/blocked/{targetUid}. Ports services/api/src/lib/blocking-service.ts. Deployed via grouped export as blocking-unblock (functions/src/blocking/manageBlocks.ts).

functions.name: crownHunt.submitClaim
functions.description: Submits a Kronjakt point claim with the full ported anti-fraud chain: feature flag, entitlement, idempotent replay (SHA-256-scoped key = claim doc ID), point availability, server-side geofence with accuracy buffer, <=1.4 m/s stopped-speed check, position freshness (<=60 s), repeat rules (once/daily/weekly), 10/day limit, rate/velocity/jump risk scoring (>=60 -> risk_review, no points). Eligibility failures return result codes with Swedish messages, not errors. Awards commit atomically with the claim record via the Kronpoäng ledger transaction. Deployed via grouped export as crownHunt-submitClaim (functions/src/crownHunt/submitClaim.ts).

functions.name: crownHunt.createPoint
functions.description: Creates a draft Kronjakt point (title <=100, geofence 20-150 m, reward 1-1000 KP, repeat rule, optional availability window). Audited. Deployed via grouped export as crownHunt-createPoint (functions/src/crownHunt/managePoints.ts).

functions.name: crownHunt.updatePoint
functions.description: Edits a draft or paused point (active/ended points are immutable); merged fields re-validated. Audited with changedFields. Deployed via grouped export as crownHunt-updatePoint (functions/src/crownHunt/managePoints.ts).

functions.name: crownHunt.activatePoint
functions.description: Safety-gated activation: requires safeLocationConfirmed and an approval note (>=3 chars) recorded in the audit entry; stamps approvedAt/approvedByUserId. Ended points cannot be activated. Deployed via grouped export as crownHunt-activatePoint (functions/src/crownHunt/managePoints.ts).

functions.name: crownHunt.pausePoint
functions.description: Pauses a point (ended points cannot be paused). Audited. Deployed via grouped export as crownHunt-pausePoint (functions/src/crownHunt/managePoints.ts).

functions.name: events.create
functions.description: Creates an event. Writes the teaser-safe events/{eventId} document and the member-gated events/{eventId}/details/private document (exact location, description) atomically. Callable by an active member OR an admin/owner (admins never need a subscription; suspended/deleted callers are rejected). An admin's event is created as a draft plus an adminAuditEvents record, published later via events.publish. A member's event is stamped createdByRole 'member' + createdByUserId, has isOfficial forced false, must clear the same publish preconditions as events.publish (future start), is published immediately (post-moderation — admins take it down with events.cancel), is capped at 3 per member per rolling 24h (resource-exhausted beyond that), and writes no adminAuditEvents record: that log stays a record of admin actions only. Deployed via grouped export as events-create (functions/src/events/manageEvent.ts).

functions.name: events.update
functions.description: Partially updates a draft or published event across both event documents; cancelled/completed events are immutable. Writes an adminAuditEvents record with changedFields. Deployed via grouped export as events-update (functions/src/events/manageEvent.ts).

functions.name: events.publish
functions.description: Publishes a draft event after validating title, approximateArea, and a future start time. Deployed via grouped export as events-publish (functions/src/events/eventLifecycle.ts).

functions.name: events.cancel
functions.description: Cancels a draft or published event with a required reason; sets cancelledAt, never hard-deletes. Deployed via grouped export as events-cancel (functions/src/events/eventLifecycle.ts).

functions.name: events.complete
functions.description: Marks a published event completed ("ended"); going-RSVP attendees receive badge attendance credit (first_event / five_events, Phase 9f). Callable by an admin/owner OR by the member who created the event (createdByUserId); any other member is permission-denied. A member ending their own event writes no adminAuditEvents record — that log stays a record of admin actions. Events also reach completed unattended a few hours after they end, via the events-autoClose scheduled sweep (functions/src/events/scheduled.ts), which applies identical semantics including the attendance credit. Deployed via grouped export as events-complete (functions/src/events/eventLifecycle.ts). SCHEDULED SIBLING - events-remindUpcoming (onSchedule, every 15 min, Europe/Stockholm; functions/src/events/eventReminders.ts): reminds going-RSVP attendees that an event they are attending starts soon. Each run finds published events starting within the next 2h (EVENT_REMINDER_LEAD_MS) that have not yet been reminded — query status=='published' AND startsAt>now AND startsAt<=now+2h ordered by startsAt, served by the EXISTING status ASC/startsAt ASC composite index (no new index) — and writes ONE in-app notification under the event_reminder category (actionType open_event, relatedEntityId=eventId) to each events/{eventId}/rsvps/{uid} whose status=='going'. Push follows automatically via notifications-onNotificationCreated; the per-category opt-out and deleted/suspended eligibility are inherited from writeInAppNotification, not re-implemented (no blocking interaction — a reminder is about an event the recipient chose to attend). AT MOST ONE reminder per (event, attendee) EVER: primary guard is a per-event marker events/{eventId}.eventReminderSentAt CLAIMED in a transaction (re-deriving the due-decision against the fresh document) before any fan-out, so exactly one run fans an event out and every later tick skips at ~one read; secondary guard is a deterministic per-event notificationId (event-reminder-{eventId}) that collapses any re-fan-out into one inbox item. The marker is set once and never cleared, so editing an event's start time (earlier or later) never double-reminds. The runEventReminders(now) runner is exported for deterministic emulator tests.

functions.name: events.postChatMessage
functions.description: Posts a plain-text message (<=1000 chars) to a published event chat. Requires an active member with a going/maybe RSVP; enforces ~5 messages/30s per user. Writes events/{eventId}/messages with denormalized author display name. Deployed via grouped export as events-postChatMessage (functions/src/events/postChatMessage.ts).

functions.name: events.reportChatMessage
functions.description: Reports a chat message (reason enum + optional details <=500 chars). Deduplicates per message+reporter+reason; own messages cannot be reported; reporter identities are never client-readable. Writes events/{eventId}/messageReports. Deployed via grouped export as events-reportChatMessage (functions/src/events/reportChatMessage.ts).

functions.name: events.removeChatMessage
functions.description: Soft-removes a chat message (moderation): blanks the member-visible body, sets moderationState removed, resolves open reports, and preserves the original text in an adminAuditEvents record. Never hard-deletes. Deployed via grouped export as events-removeChatMessage (functions/src/events/removeChatMessage.ts).

functions.name: events.listChatReports
functions.description: Admin chat-report moderation queue. events/{eventId}/messageReports is backend-only (rules read/write:false), so this Admin-SDK collectionGroup scan is the only admin read path. Returns reports newest-first, ordered by the messageReports/createdAt DESC collectionGroup index over a bounded scan (single window, optional status refinement, pageSize<=100 — no page cursor yet), each including eventId + reporterUserId (surfaced to admins only). Deployed via grouped export as events-listChatReports (functions/src/events/moderateReports.ts).

functions.name: events.resolveChatReport
functions.description: Transitions one chat report to under_review/resolved/dismissed, stamping reviewedByUserId + reviewedAt and writing an adminAuditEvents record. not-found when the report is absent. Removing the offending message is the separate events.removeChatMessage callable (which also auto-resolves open reports). Deployed via grouped export as events-resolveChatReport (functions/src/events/moderateReports.ts).

functions.name: garage.addVehicle
functions.description: Adds a vehicle to the caller's garage (max 5 per user, enforced transactionally). Strict schema: make/model/modelYear/powertrain/engineDescription/description/color only — registration numbers, VIN, insurance, and location are unrepresentable because vehicles/{vehicleId} is authenticated-readable. Deployed via grouped export as garage-addVehicle (functions/src/garage/manageVehicle.ts).

functions.name: garage.updateVehicle
functions.description: Partially updates an owned vehicle, including setting/clearing imagePath (validated against the caller's own vehicleImages/{uid}/{vehicleId}/ prefix). Ownership failures return not-found to avoid existence probing. Deployed via grouped export as garage-updateVehicle (functions/src/garage/manageVehicle.ts).

functions.name: garage.setMainVehicle
functions.description: Marks (or clears) one owned vehicle as the caller's main car. At most one main car per user is enforced transactionally — setting one clears any other. Ownership failures return not-found to avoid existence probing. Deployed via grouped export as garage-setMainVehicle (functions/src/garage/manageVehicle.ts).

functions.name: garage.deleteVehicle
functions.description: Deletes an owned vehicle: removes the vehicleImages/{uid}/{vehicleId}/ storage prefix first, then the document. Deployed via grouped export as garage-deleteVehicle (functions/src/garage/manageVehicle.ts).

functions.name: garage.addVehiclePhoto
functions.description: Appends one already-uploaded photo path to an owned vehicle's photoPaths gallery (max 10; own vehicleImages/{uid}/{vehicleId}/ prefix validated like updateVehicle's imagePath). imagePath mirrors the cover (photoPaths[0]); a first photo becomes the cover. failed-precondition at the cap, already-exists for a duplicate, not-found for a foreign/missing vehicle. Deployed via grouped export as garage-addVehiclePhoto (functions/src/garage/manageVehicle.ts).

functions.name: garage.removeVehiclePhoto
functions.description: Removes one photo path from an owned vehicle's photoPaths and deletes its Storage object; removing the cover promotes the next remaining photo. imagePath is kept in sync with photoPaths[0]. not-found when the path is not on the vehicle. Deployed via grouped export as garage-removeVehiclePhoto (functions/src/garage/manageVehicle.ts).

functions.name: garage.reorderVehiclePhotos
functions.description: Sets the full display order of an owned vehicle's photos; orderedPaths must be a permutation of the current set and orderedPaths[0] becomes the cover (mirrored into imagePath). invalid-argument when not a permutation. Deployed via grouped export as garage-reorderVehiclePhotos (functions/src/garage/manageVehicle.ts).

functions.name: badges.awardHelpfulMember
functions.description: Manually awards the helpful_member badge (the only manually awardable key). Requires a non-empty reason; writes an adminAuditEvents record on first award only; idempotent repeats never duplicate audit entries; suspended/deleted targets rejected. Deployed via grouped export as badges-awardHelpfulMember (functions/src/badges/awardHelpfulMember.ts).

functions.name: badges.adminSummary
functions.description: Returns aggregate badge award counts per catalog key (totalCount + last-30-day recentCount), ordered by the catalog. Aggregate-only — no leaderboard or individual user data. Badges live at users/{uid}/badges/{badgeKey} (owner-only, NOT admin-readable via rules), so the summary is computed with the Admin SDK over a collectionGroup scan. Ports the legacy SQL groupBy. Deployed via grouped export as badges-adminSummary (functions/src/badges/adminSummary.ts).

functions.name: points.adminAdjust
functions.description: Admin Kronpoäng adjustment (credit or debit): positive integer amount, mandatory reason (<=500), debits never overdraft, only an owner may adjust another owner. Runs through the internal transaction primitives and writes an adminAuditEvents record. Deployed via grouped export as points-adminAdjust (functions/src/points/adminPoints.ts).

functions.name: points.adminReverse
functions.description: Reverses a ledger entry with a compensating reversal entry (deterministic ID: one reversal per original, replay-safe). Reversals cannot be reversed; an overdrafting reversal is rejected; writes an adminAuditEvents record in the same transaction. Deployed via grouped export as points-adminReverse (functions/src/points/adminPoints.ts).

functions.name: partners.submitApplication
functions.description: Submits a partner application (contact data, never client-readable). Duplicate-spam guard: one active application per user or contact email. Deployed via grouped export as partners-submitApplication (functions/src/partners/applications.ts).

functions.name: partners.reviewApplication
functions.description: Admin review flow: start_review, approve (creates the draft company in the same transaction, idempotent), or reject (note required). Every step audited. Deployed via grouped export as partners-reviewApplication (functions/src/partners/applications.ts).

functions.name: partners.createCompany
functions.description: Creates a draft partner company (legacy field limits; logoPath under companyImages/{companyId}/). Audited. Deployed via grouped export as partners-createCompany (functions/src/partners/manageCompany.ts).

functions.name: partners.updateCompany
functions.description: Edits a draft or paused company (active/ended are immutable). Audited with changedFields. Deployed via grouped export as partners-updateCompany (functions/src/partners/manageCompany.ts).

functions.name: partners.setCompanyStatus
functions.description: Company lifecycle transitions: activate | pause | end (ended is terminal). Audited. Deployed via grouped export as partners-setCompanyStatus (functions/src/partners/manageCompany.ts).

functions.name: partners.createOffer
functions.description: Creates a draft offer with the three-tier privacy split: teaser document, member detail subdocument, and the backend-only discount code. Audited (the code value never appears in audit details). Deployed via grouped export as partners-createOffer (functions/src/partners/manageOffer.ts).

functions.name: partners.updateOffer
functions.description: Edits a draft or paused offer across the three documents; merged availability window re-validated. Audited with changedFields (names only). Deployed via grouped export as partners-updateOffer (functions/src/partners/manageOffer.ts).

functions.name: partners.setOfferStatus
functions.description: Offer lifecycle transitions: activate | pause | end (ended/expired are terminal). Audited. Deployed via grouped export as partners-setOfferStatus (functions/src/partners/manageOffer.ts).

functions.name: partners.showOfferCode
functions.description: Reveals an active offer's discount code to an active member — the ONLY place the code ever appears; never logged (legacy rule). Deployed via grouped export as partners-showOfferCode (functions/src/partners/manageOffer.ts).

functions.name: partnerInsights.recordInteraction
functions.description: Records one partner interaction event with a PARTNER-SCOPED user hash (raw UIDs never stored), deduped to one event per company+type+UTC-day+user via a deterministic document ID. anonymous_pass_by requires the partnerInsightsPassBy flag (contract default OFF) AND the caller's anonymousPartnerStatsOptIn — non-opted-in contributions return { recorded: false } silently so opting out is unobservable. Events expire after 7 days; the scheduled partnerInsights-aggregateDaily writes threshold-enforced aggregates (min 10 unique contributors for pass-by, config can only raise) and partnerInsights-cleanupExpired removes expired raw events. Deployed via grouped export as partnerInsights-recordInteraction (functions/src/partnerInsights/recordInteraction.ts).

functions.name: partnerInsights.adminSummary
functions.description: The only read path for partner insights (partnerInsights and partnerInsightsEvents are backend-only, read/write:false, even for admins). Returns the threshold-enforced per-interaction-type aggregates for one company + period (day/week/month, defaulting to the last aggregated day). Looks up aggregates by deterministic id via getAll (no index); re-applies the minimum-unique-contributor floor at read time as defense in depth (an available anonymous_pass_by row below the floor is re-zeroed to insufficient_data). No user-level data is ever returned. Deployed via grouped export as partnerInsights-adminSummary (functions/src/partnerInsights/adminSummary.ts).

functions.name: billboards.create
functions.description: Creates a draft sponsored billboard for an existing partner (headline <=100, message <=300, placement enum, coordinates, optional CTA pair + safety note + image under billboardImages/{billboardId}/). Audited. Deployed via grouped export as billboards-create (functions/src/billboards/manageBillboard.ts).

functions.name: billboards.update
functions.description: Edits a draft or paused billboard (active/ended immutable); merged CTA pair and availability window re-validated. Audited with changedFields. Deployed via grouped export as billboards-update (functions/src/billboards/manageBillboard.ts).

functions.name: billboards.activate
functions.description: SAFETY GATE: requires ALL six safety confirmations (not a business location, not a road lane, not a road sign, not obstructing the map, marked as advertising, suitable for the map) plus an approval reason recorded in the audit entry; the sponsoring partner must be ACTIVE; stamps approvedAt/approvedByUserId. Deployed via grouped export as billboards-activate (functions/src/billboards/manageBillboard.ts).

functions.name: billboards.setStatus
functions.description: Pauses or ends a billboard (ended is terminal). Audited. Deployed via grouped export as billboards-setStatus (functions/src/billboards/manageBillboard.ts).

functions.name: billboards.recordInteraction
functions.description: Records a billboard tap (impression/open/navigate/phone/website/offer_view), mapped onto partner-insights interaction types and written through the 9j privacy pipeline (scoped hashes, per-day dedupe, 7-day TTL). Gated by the digitalBillboards flag; analytics failure never blocks the action. Deployed via grouped export as billboards-recordInteraction (functions/src/billboards/manageBillboard.ts).

functions.name: notifications.markRead
functions.description: Marks one in-app notification as read. The inbox (notifications/{uid}/items) is backend-write-only, so read-state changes go through this callable; ownership is structural (only the caller's own inbox is touched — another user's notification ID is not-found). Idempotent: replays return marked=false. Deployed via grouped export as notifications-markRead (functions/src/notifications/manageNotifications.ts).

functions.name: notifications.markAllRead
functions.description: Marks all of the caller's unread notifications as read (batched) and returns markedCount. Idempotent. Deployed via grouped export as notifications-markAllRead (functions/src/notifications/manageNotifications.ts).

functions.name: notifications.registerPushToken
functions.description: Registers a push device token. The raw FCM token is stored in the userPrivate/{uid}/pushTokens document (FCM addresses a device BY the token, so a hash-only registry cannot send); the SHA-256 hash remains the document ID, which keeps registration idempotent — re-registers bump lastSeenAt. Multiple devices per member are supported (one document per token). The raw token is never logged and never returned: the response carries only the tokenId hash, and the collection denies ALL client access in firestore.rules. Gated by the pushNotifications feature flag. Deployed via grouped export as notifications-registerPushToken (functions/src/notifications/pushTokens.ts).

functions.name: notifications.adminSend
functions.description: Admin batch in-app notification send. Resolves an audience (all_users/free_users/members/admins/specific_user/event_participants), then fans an in-app notification out via writeInAppNotification (skips deleted/suspended recipients and honours per-category in-app opt-outs; essential categories always deliver). Idempotent per idempotencyKey (deterministic batchId; a replay is already-exists). Broad audiences (all_users/free_users) require confirmed:true. Synchronous fan-out bounded by 500 (larger audiences rejected). Mandatory reason is written to adminAuditEvents. Push follows automatically for every delivered item via the notifications-onNotificationCreated trigger. Deployed via grouped export as notifications-adminSend (functions/src/notifications/adminSend.ts).

functions.name: notifications.unregisterPushToken
functions.description: Deletes a push token registration by tokenId. Requires authentication only — suspended users may clean up their devices (legacy parity). Idempotent: returns removed=false when the registration does not exist. Deployed via grouped export as notifications-unregisterPushToken (functions/src/notifications/pushTokens.ts).

functions.name: diagnostics.submitReport
functions.description: Submits a crash/error report into diagnosticsReports (admin-only read). PUBLIC: anonymous reports are allowed (sign-in failures must be reportable). App Check is INTENTIONALLY NON-ENFORCING on this callable ONLY (unlike every other callable): the pre-auth telemetry path must still work on devices that cannot yet mint a Play Integrity token — the exact case it exists to surface. A valid token is still verified best-effort and recorded (appCheckPresent); a missing/invalid one no longer blocks the write. Abuse is bounded because writes land only in the admin-read-only private diagnosticsReports collection (90-day retention), all payloads are server-sanitized (tokens/credentials/coordinates/stack-trace keys stripped, bounded scalars only, SHA-256 dedup fingerprint), and the only public effect — the diagnostics-onSignInFailure auto-issue — is independently bounded by an allowlist + single Unknown bucket + per-fingerprint dedup. Deployed via grouped export as diagnostics-submitReport (functions/src/diagnostics/submitReport.ts).

functions.name: feedback.reportIssue
functions.description: Android "Report a problem" flow. AUTHENTICATED (non-suspended, non-deleted): unauthenticated callers are rejected with unauthenticated. Rate-limited to 5 reports/hour/user (resource-exhausted when exceeded). Persists the PRIVATE record of record to feedbackReports/{reportId} (admin-only read; carries the uid + client context + timestamp) FIRST so a report is never lost, then files a PUBLIC GitHub issue (labelled android-issue) on SebMcCayen/carcommunity via REST using the GITHUB_ISSUE_TOKEN secret. PUBLIC-REPO SAFETY: the issue body carries the user-entered description (public — the in-app UI warns users not to include personal info, and the backend does not scrub free text) plus only non-identifying context: appVersion/osVersion/deviceModel, the server report id and the submitted-at timestamp. The backend never attaches the caller's uid or any other server-side account identifier to the public issue. GitHub failures mark the doc githubIssueStatus:'failed' but still return success (never surfacing a raw GitHub error). Deployed via grouped export as feedback-reportIssue (functions/src/feedback/reportIssue.ts).

functions.name: errors.reportClientError
functions.description: Reports a genuine client-side RUNTIME error (e.g. the Messages inbox listener failing). AUTHENTICATED (non-suspended, non-deleted; no member entitlement required): unauthenticated callers are rejected with unauthenticated (pre-auth failures use diagnostics.submitReport). Rate-limited to 30 reports/hour/user (resource-exhausted when exceeded). Persists the PRIVATE record of record to clientErrorReports/{reportId} (admin-only read; carries the uid + bounded error context) FIRST, then writes an adminAuditEvents entry (action client.error, adminId=uid, targetId=fingerprint) so the error shows in the admin Audit Log. The errors-onClientErrorReport Firestore trigger then files ONE deduplicated PUBLIC GitHub issue per unique fingerprint (labelled auto-error + auto-generated) via the GITHUB_ISSUE_TOKEN secret, tallying occurrences in the server-only clientErrorIssueLinks/{fingerprint} collection so a recurring error never spams issues. PUBLIC-REPO SAFETY: the issue body carries only the feature key + app-generated message/code + non-identifying client context + fingerprint; the uid is NEVER attached to the public issue (it stays in the admin-only clientErrorReports doc + audit details). Deployed via grouped export as errors-reportClientError (functions/src/errors/reportClientError.ts).

functions.name: account.deleteAccount
functions.description: Immediate soft delete (stage 1 of the two-stage deletion workflow): disables the Firebase Auth user and revokes refresh tokens FIRST (fail-safe ordering), then writes accountDeletionRequests/{uid} (status pending) and users/{uid}.deleted=true atomically. Idempotent — repeat calls return the pending request. signedIn access: works while suspended (deletion is a support path). The hard purge runs after the 30-day retention window via the scheduled account-purgeDeleted (Firestore trees, owned vehicles/rides, storage prefixes, the Auth user; moderation/audit history is deliberately retained and the request record becomes the proof-of-deletion). Deployed via grouped export as account-deleteAccount (functions/src/account/deleteAccount.ts).

functions.name: subscription.grantEntitlement
functions.description: Audited manual entitlement grant/revoke (platform manual, reserved by the legacy enum) - the operational path until store receipt verification is wired. Applies the full chain with Phase 8 fail-safe privilege ordering: subscriptions/{uid} record, users/{uid}.activeMember, and the activeMember custom claim (revokes also revoke refresh tokens). Deployed via grouped export as subscription-grantEntitlement (functions/src/subscription/verify.ts).

functions.name: groupDrive.join
functions.description: Joins the caller to an event group drive roster (events/{eventId}/groupDriveParticipants/{uid}). Requires a published, not-ended event and an RSVP of going or maybe (legacy canJoinEventGroupDrive). Idempotent; a left participant rejoins with joinedAt reset. displayName denormalized for the roster. Deployed via grouped export as groupDrive-join (functions/src/groupDrive/participants.ts).

functions.name: groupDrive.updateStatus
functions.description: Updates the caller's group drive status (joined|on_the_way|arrived - never left; leave is its own operation). Requires an active participation. Deployed via grouped export as groupDrive-updateStatus (functions/src/groupDrive/participants.ts).

functions.name: groupDrive.leave
functions.description: Marks the caller as left on the roster (idempotent; leaving when absent succeeds quietly). Does NOT stop the live location session (legacy parity). Works with lapsed entitlement (authenticated, not member). Deployed via grouped export as groupDrive-leave (functions/src/groupDrive/participants.ts).

functions.name: admin.suspendUser
functions.description: Suspends a user (moderation): sets the suspended custom claim, mirrors users/{uid}.suspended, and writes immutable moderationActions and adminAuditEvents records with actor, target, reason, and server timestamp. Deployed via grouped export as admin-suspendUser (functions/src/admin/suspendUser.ts).

functions.name: admin.warnUser
functions.description: Issues a formal warning: immutable moderationActions record (type warning) + user.warn adminAuditEvents record committed atomically, and a best-effort essential account_warning in-app notification attempted via the notifications writer (non-blocking — a delivery failure never fails the callable; delivered even to suspended users). Not idempotent across retries: each call writes a fresh moderation action + notice. Deliberate deviation from legacy: no users/{uid} status change — the target model has no warned access state and a warning never restricts access. Owner accounts can only be moderated by owners. Deployed via grouped export as admin-warnUser (functions/src/admin/warnUser.ts).

functions.name: admin.restoreAccess
functions.description: Restores a suspended user: clears the suspended custom claim, mirrors users/{uid}.suspended, and writes immutable moderationActions and adminAuditEvents records. Deployed via grouped export as admin-restoreAccess (functions/src/admin/restoreAccess.ts).

functions.name: admin.setFeatureFlag
functions.description: Sets one boolean flag on the flat config/featureFlags document (merge-set; other flags untouched). The key must be in the canonical list in contracts/features/feature-flags.json — the namespace is closed, unknown keys are invalid-argument. The write commits atomically with an adminAuditEvents record. Clients read the document directly (authenticated, rules-gated) and fall back to contract defaults. Deployed via grouped export as admin-setFeatureFlag (functions/src/admin/setFeatureFlag.ts).

functions.name: admin.setAdminRole
functions.description: Grants or revokes the admin custom claim and mirrors it to users/{uid}.role. No client self-elevation: callers can never change their own role, and owner accounts are never modified. Writes an immutable adminAuditEvents record. Deployed via grouped export as admin-setAdminRole (functions/src/admin/setAdminRole.ts).

functions.name: friend.sendRequest
functions.description: Sends a friend request to a user resolved by nickname (displayName, NOT unique) or by a resolved toUid. Nickname resolution: 0 matches → not-found, 1 → proceed, >1 → failed-precondition with reason AMBIGUOUS_NICKNAME and a candidates:[{uid,displayName,avatarPath}] list in the error details, so the client re-calls with { toUid }. Rejects self (invalid-argument), already-friends and an existing pending outgoing request (already-exists), and either-way blocks (failed-precondition NOT_ADDABLE, neutral so the block direction is never revealed). If the target already has a PENDING request to the caller, the two are befriended immediately (returns status 'friends'). Writes friendRequests/{requestId} where requestId is a collision-resistant length-prefixed SHA-256 over the ordered (fromUid, toUid) pair. Deployed via grouped export as friend-sendRequest (functions/src/friends/manageFriends.ts).

functions.name: friend.respondRequest
functions.description: Accepts or declines a PENDING friend request addressed to the caller ({ requestId, action: 'accept'|'decline' }). Only the recipient (toUid) may respond; a non-recipient or missing request is not-found (never permission-denied, so requests can't be probed); an already-handled request is failed-precondition. Accept writes users/{uid}/friends/{friendUid} for BOTH sides (re-reading live profiles) and marks the request accepted; decline marks it declined. Deployed via grouped export as friend-respondRequest (functions/src/friends/manageFriends.ts).

functions.name: friend.remove
functions.description: Removes an established friend ({ friendUid }). Idempotent: deletes users/{caller}/friends/{friendUid} and the mirror users/{friendUid}/friends/{caller}; returns { removed } reflecting whether the caller's own side existed (self is always { removed: false }). Established friendship — not request status — is the source of truth, so a later friend.sendRequest can re-friend. Deployed via grouped export as friend-remove (functions/src/friends/manageFriends.ts).

functions.name: friend.list
functions.description: Lists the caller's established friends plus incoming and outgoing PENDING requests ({} input). Returns { friends:[{uid,displayName,avatarPath,friendsSince}], incoming:[FriendRequestSummary], outgoing:[FriendRequestSummary] } where each FriendRequestSummary is { requestId, fromUid, toUid, direction, otherUser:{uid,displayName,avatarPath}, createdAt } with the OTHER party projected for the UI. Owner-only server reads; friends are also directly owner-readable at users/{uid}/friends. Each of the three queries is bounded (friends capped at 1000, incoming/outgoing pending each capped at 500) so a large friend graph can't cause an unbounded read; cursor pagination is a possible follow-up without changing the response shape. Deployed via grouped export as friend-list (functions/src/friends/manageFriends.ts).

functions.name: dm.sendMessage
functions.description: Sends a 1:1 direct message to an ESTABLISHED friend ({ toUid, text, clientId? }, text 1..2000). Requires an established friendship (users/{uid}/friends/{friendUid}) — else failed-precondition NOT_FRIENDS; rejects self (invalid-argument) and either-way blocks (failed-precondition, neutral). Creates or updates the canonical conversations/{pairId} (pairId = the two UIDs sorted + joined by `__`), appends conversations/{pairId}/messages/{id} {senderUid,text,createdAt,clientId?}, bumps the recipient's per-member unread AND the userPrivate/{recipient}.dmUnreadTotal aggregate in one transaction. Returns { conversationId, messageId }. The optional clientId is a client idempotency key ([A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}, e.g. a UUID) used verbatim as the message doc id so an optimistic-send retry is exactly-once (a resend of the same clientId returns the existing messageId without re-bumping unread or re-notifying) and the live listener can reconcile the delivered doc against the optimistic bubble; messageId equals clientId when supplied. FCM push deferred to end-of-MVP. Deployed via grouped export as dm-sendMessage (functions/src/dm/manageDirectMessages.ts).

functions.name: dm.listConversations
functions.description: Lists the caller's DM conversations newest-first ({} input). Returns { conversations:[{ conversationId, otherUser:{uid,displayName,avatarPath}, lastMessage:{text,senderUid,createdAt}|null, unreadCount, lastReadAt }], totalUnread }. otherUser + lastMessage are denormalized on conversations/{pairId}; unreadCount/lastReadAt are the caller's own per-member values. totalUnread mirrors userPrivate/{uid}.dmUnreadTotal (the badge source). Deployed via grouped export as dm-listConversations (functions/src/dm/manageDirectMessages.ts).

functions.name: dm.getMessages
functions.description: Paginated newest-first messages for a conversation ({ conversationId, before? } where before is an ISO-8601 createdAt cursor, exclusive). Only a member of the pair may read; a non-member or missing conversation is not-found (never permission-denied, so conversations can't be probed). Returns { conversationId, messages:[{id,senderUid,text,createdAt}], nextBefore, hasMore } (page size 30). Deployed via grouped export as dm-getMessages (functions/src/dm/manageDirectMessages.ts).

functions.name: dm.markRead
functions.description: Clears the caller's unread for a conversation ({ conversationId }). Sets conversations/{pairId}.unread[caller]=0 + lastReadAt[caller]=now and decrements userPrivate/{caller}.dmUnreadTotal by exactly the cleared amount (never underflows) in one transaction. Non-member/missing → not-found. Returns { conversationId, cleared }. Deployed via grouped export as dm-markRead (functions/src/dm/manageDirectMessages.ts).

functions.name: dm.reportMessage
functions.description: Reports a message in a 1:1 DM conversation ({ conversationId, messageId, reason: harassment|hate_or_abuse|spam|unsafe_driving|privacy|other, details? <=500 chars }). Caller must be one of the conversation's two members; a missing conversation and a conversation the caller isn't in both return not-found (parity with dm.getMessages, so the endpoint can't probe whether two people talk). Reporting your own message is invalid-argument. Ids are constrained to a single Firestore document-id segment (no `/`, no `.`/`..`, no reserved `__*__`) so a hostile id is invalid-argument rather than a traversal into another document. BLOCKING does NOT gate reporting either way. SNAPSHOTS the reported message (text + author uid/displayName + createdAt) into the report because DM messages are readable only by the two participants — rules give admins no read path into conversations, so a report holding only ids would be unactionable; exactly one message is copied, never the thread. Deduplicates per conversation+message+reporter+reason (repeat silently refreshes details only; never resets a report a moderator already actioned, and the response never reveals a prior report existed). Rate-limited to 10 NEW reports/hour/reporter across all report types (resource-exhausted). Writes moderationReports/{reportId} (admin-read-only, client-write-denied). Returns { reported: true }. Deployed via grouped export as dm-reportMessage (functions/src/dm/reportMessage.ts).

functions.name: convoy.create
functions.description: Creates a convoy and invites a list of the owner's FRIENDS ({ inviteeUids:[uid] (1..50), title? (1..80) }). Each invitee is validated: must be an established friend (users/{owner}/friends/{uid}), not blocked either way, and a non-restricted existing account — non-friend/blocked/missing/self/duplicate invitees are silently SKIPPED (never an error that would reveal a block). Writes convoys/{convoyId} (status 'forming') with the owner seeded as members[owner]={role:'owner',inviteStatus:'accepted'} and each accepted invitee as {role:'member',inviteStatus:'invited'}; memberUids=[owner,...invitees] drives the list read + rules gate; memberProfiles denormalized. Writes a best-effort in-app notification per invitee (system_notice category). Returns { convoy: ConvoySummary, invited:[uid], skipped:[{uid,reason}] } where reason is self|not_friend|not_found|duplicate (a block edge either way is surfaced as the neutral not_found, so the inviter can't infer who blocked whom). failed-precondition if no invitee is valid. Deployed via grouped export as convoy-create (functions/src/convoy/manageConvoy.ts).

functions.name: convoy.respond
functions.description: An invitee accepts or declines their convoy invite ({ convoyId, action:'accept'|'decline' }). Only an invitee (members[caller].role=='member') with a still-pending invite may respond; a non-member or missing convoy is not-found (never permission-denied, so convoys can't be probed); an already-answered invite or an ended convoy is failed-precondition. Accept sets members[caller].inviteStatus='accepted' + joinedAt=now (the green dot); decline sets 'declined'. Returns { convoy: ConvoySummary, inviteStatus }. Deployed via grouped export as convoy-respond (functions/src/convoy/manageConvoy.ts).

functions.name: convoy.start
functions.description: The owner transitions a convoy forming → active ({ convoyId }), setting startedAt. Owner-only: a non-owner (including a member) is not-found (can't probe); a convoy not in 'forming' is failed-precondition. Returns { convoy: ConvoySummary }. Deployed via grouped export as convoy-start (functions/src/convoy/manageConvoy.ts).

functions.name: convoy.end
functions.description: The owner ends a convoy ({ convoyId }) → status 'ended', endedAt set, and a summary computed + stored on the doc (durationSeconds from startedAt→endedAt, participantUids/participantCount = accepted members, distanceMeters null — no shared-route aggregation in this foundation). The summary is readable by ALL members (they read the convoy doc). Owner-only (else not-found); an already-ended convoy is failed-precondition. Returns { convoy: ConvoySummary }. Deployed via grouped export as convoy-end (functions/src/convoy/manageConvoy.ts).

functions.name: convoy.list
functions.description: Lists the caller's convoys ({} input): { convoys:[ConvoySummary], pendingInvites:[ConvoySummary] } newest-first (bounded at 200 via the [memberUids CONTAINS, createdAt DESC] index). pendingInvites is the subset the caller still has a pending invite for (non-ended + viewer.inviteStatus=='invited'). ConvoySummary = { convoyId, ownerUid, title, status, members:[{uid,role,inviteStatus,joinedAt,displayName,avatarPath}] (inviteStatus is the green dot), memberUids, viewer:{role,inviteStatus}|null, livePositionUids:[uid] (accepted members — the uids the map subscribes to at RTDB liveLocation/{uid}/latest for live positions), destination:{latitude,longitude,label,setByUid,setByDisplayName,setAt}|null (the shared destination — see convoy.setDestination; survives end), summary:{durationSeconds,participantUids,participantCount,distanceMeters}|null, createdAt, startedAt, endedAt }. Deployed via grouped export as convoy-list (functions/src/convoy/manageConvoy.ts).

functions.name: convoy.leave
functions.description: An ACCEPTED non-owner member removes THEMSELVES from a convoy ({ convoyId }). Fills the gap convoy.respond cannot: respond hard-requires members[caller].inviteStatus=='invited' and throws failed-precondition once you have accepted. The caller's entry is deleted from members + memberProfiles and their uid removed from memberUids (all three written whole in one transaction), so their convoy read (rules gate on memberUids), their convoy chat access and their livePositionUids slot all drop together. The OWNER is refused with failed-precondition and must use convoy.end — an owner leaving would orphan every owner-gated transition (start/end/summary) with no succession rule. A still-invited or declined member is also failed-precondition (nothing to leave; respond is their path); an ended convoy is failed-precondition; a non-member / unknown convoy is not-found (never permission-denied, so a convoy can't be probed). The LAST non-owner leaving does NOT auto-end the convoy — it is left alive with the owner alone, because ending writes the permanent shared summary and is the owner's deliberate act. Returns { convoy: ConvoySummary (built from the post-transaction state; viewer is null — the caller is no longer a member), remainingMemberCount }. Deployed via grouped export as convoy-leave (functions/src/convoy/manageConvoy.ts).

functions.name: convoy.invite
functions.description: Adds invitees to an EXISTING convoy ({ convoyId, inviteeUids: [uid] (1..25) }) as members[uid]={role:'member',inviteStatus:'invited'} — convoy.create takes invitees only at creation, so without this a convoy can never grow. ANY ACCEPTED member may invite, not the owner alone: a convoy is a peer group and the owner is frequently the one driving, so owner-only would make the common case (adding the friend who just phoned) impossible; every candidate must still be an established FRIEND of the INVITER (users/{inviter}/friends/{uid}), which is what keeps 'any member' from meaning 'any stranger'. Blocking is honoured both ways against the inviter AND against every other ACCEPTED member, so nobody can be pulled into a convoy with someone who blocked them. Skip reasons are the same neutral set as convoy.create plus already_member (uid already in memberUids); a block edge is surfaced as the neutral not_found. Bounded: max 25 invitees per call and a hard cap of 25 TOTAL members (MAX_CONVOY_SIZE) — an over-cap batch is refused WHOLE (failed-precondition) rather than partially applied. Membership + cap are re-asserted inside the transaction and memberUids grows via arrayUnion, so concurrent invites/leaves cannot clobber each other. IDEMPOTENT: if every requested uid is already in the convoy — including when a CONCURRENT invite added them mid-call — the call SUCCEEDS with invited:[] and reason already_member, because the post-state asked for is the post-state that exists. Ended convoy / caller not accepted / no requested uid addable AND none already a member → failed-precondition; non-member or unknown convoy → not-found. Writes the same best-effort in-app 'convoy_invite' notification per added invitee as convoy.create (one shared path, so an invitee's opt-out works identically). Returns { convoy: ConvoySummary, invited:[uid], skipped:[{uid,reason}] }. Deployed via grouped export as convoy-invite (functions/src/convoy/manageConvoy.ts).

functions.name: convoy.setDestination
functions.description: Sets or REPLACES the convoy's SHARED DESTINATION ({ convoyId, latitude, longitude, label? }) — the one place every member can start navigation to. Any ACCEPTED member may set it (not owner-only: the owner is frequently driving and the person who knows where the meet is often isn't whoever pressed create); last write wins, with the whole destination object written atomically so a new coordinate is never observable paired with the previous label. Server-validated: latitude finite in [-90,90], longitude finite in [-180,180] (NaN/Infinity explicitly rejected — they survive JSON round-trips and would poison downstream distance math), label trimmed and max 120 chars (over-length is invalid-argument, never silent truncation; blank-after-trim stored as ABSENT, not ''). setByUid comes from the verified auth context and setAt from the server clock — never client-supplied, or a member could attribute a destination to someone else; setByDisplayName is denormalized from memberProfiles like members[].displayName. A 'forming' convoy MAY have a destination (agreeing where to go is what happens before rolling); 'ended' → failed-precondition; caller not accepted → failed-precondition; non-member / unknown convoy → not-found (never permission-denied). Members READ it as ConvoySummary.destination on the convoy read path they already use — no new listener, no second source of truth. ARRIVAL is deliberately NOT tracked and NEVER auto-ends the convoy. Returns { convoy: ConvoySummary }. Deployed via grouped export as convoy-setDestination (functions/src/convoy/manageConvoy.ts).

functions.name: convoy.clearDestination
functions.description: Clears the convoy's shared destination ({ convoyId }), deleting the `destination` field. Permitted to the member who SET it or the convoy OWNER — clearing is strictly more destructive than replacing (it can leave members mid-drive with nothing to navigate to and leaves no replacement to explain itself), so setter-or-owner lets the person who made the mess undo it and gives the owner a moderation path without letting any member wipe a plan the group is following. Any other accepted member → permission-denied (they already know the convoy exists, so not-found would mislead). Clearing when nothing is set is an idempotent NO-OP, not an error (two people tapping at once is normal). Ended convoy → failed-precondition: the destination SURVIVES convoy.end untouched as a record of where the group was headed, so there is nothing live to clear. Caller not accepted → failed-precondition; non-member / unknown convoy → not-found. Returns { convoy: ConvoySummary }. Deployed via grouped export as convoy-clearDestination (functions/src/convoy/manageConvoy.ts).

functions.name: communityChat.post
functions.description: Posts a message to the single APP-WIDE community chat ({ text, mentionedUids? }, text 1..2000, mentionedUids at most 10 uids). Member-gated (active member; else permission-denied); rejects empty/oversize text and more than 10 mentionedUids (invalid-argument). Appends communityChat/global/messages/{id} {senderUid, text, createdAt, senderDisplayName, senderAvatarPath, mentionedUids} — the sender's safe profile is denormalized onto the message so the channel renders with no per-message profile lookup. @MENTIONS are resolved CLIENT-SIDE (displayName is NOT unique, so the server never parses names out of the text and guesses): the client's @-picker sends uids and the server VALIDATES them — dedup, drop self-mentions, drop uids that aren't deliverable active members, drop pairs blocked either way (all drops, never a rejection: those are races and must not fail the post). The surviving set is stored as mentionedUids (always present, [] when none) for client highlighting AND is the ONLY community_chat notification fan-out: each surviving uid gets an in-app 'community_chat' notice (per-category opt-out honoured by writeInAppNotification) with relatedEntityId = the message id; a message with no mentions notifies NOBODY. A deterministic per-(sender, 15-min window) notification id caps a repeat-mentioner at one notice per window per recipient. Backend is the sole writer (firebase/firestore.rules grants any active-member read, denies client writes). Returns { messageId, mentionedUids } (the accepted mention set). FCM push deferred to end-of-MVP. Deployed via grouped export as communityChat-post (functions/src/chatchannels/communityChat.ts).

functions.name: communityChat.list
functions.description: Paginated newest-first community messages ({ before? } where before is an ISO-8601 createdAt cursor, exclusive). Any active member reads. Returns { messages:[{id,senderUid,text,senderDisplayName,senderAvatarPath,mentionedUids,createdAt}], nextBefore, hasMore, lastReadAt } (page size 30). mentionedUids is the server-validated @mention set for the message ([] when none, and for messages posted before mentions existed) — the client highlights those uids without resolving anything. lastReadAt is the caller's own userPrivate/{uid}.communityChatLastReadAt marker (the client derives the unread dot by comparing the newest message's createdAt to it — no fan-out unread aggregate). Blocking is NOT filtered server-side (global town square). Deployed via grouped export as communityChat-list (functions/src/chatchannels/communityChat.ts).

functions.name: communityChat.markRead
functions.description: Stamps the caller's community last-read marker ({} input) at userPrivate/{uid}.communityChatLastReadAt = now (owner-only readable, alongside dmUnreadTotal). The client's newest-message live listener uses it to show/clear the unread dot (O(1) per user, no fan-out). This same marker is the signal consumed by the scheduled community-chat DIGEST (see below). Returns { lastReadAt }. Deployed via grouped export as communityChat-markRead (functions/src/chatchannels/communityChat.ts). SCHEDULED SIBLING - communityChat-digest (onSchedule, 18:00 Europe/Stockholm, daily; functions/src/chatchannels/communityDigest.ts): the community channel has NO per-message notification producer (its audience is every active member, so per-message notify is O(members x messages) spam); besides @mentions, the DIGEST is how a member who was not mentioned still hears the channel was busy. Each run writes at most ONE in-app notification under the community_chat category to each member whose communityChatLastReadAt is behind the newest message by >= COMMUNITY_DIGEST_MIN_UNREAD (3) messages. Cost is O(behind-members) per DAY (a userPrivate last-read range query + one count() aggregation per behind member - the messages themselves are never fetched, and caught-up members are never read), NOT per message. Double-notify is prevented by a per-member digest marker userPrivate/{uid}.communityChatDigestedUpTo (advanced to the run's newest instant on notify) plus a per-UTC-day deterministic notificationId; the per-category opt-out and deleted/suspended eligibility are inherited from writeInAppNotification, not re-implemented. No new Firestore index is required (both queries use automatic single-field indexes).

functions.name: convoyChat.post
functions.description: Posts a message to a per-CONVOY chat ({ convoyId, text }, text 1..2000). Member-gated AND accepted-convoy-member-gated: the caller must be in convoys/{convoyId}.memberUids with members[caller].inviteStatus=='accepted' (owner seeded accepted). A missing convoy or a total outsider is not-found (never permission-denied, so a convoy can't be probed); a still-invited/declined member is failed-precondition. Appends convoyChats/{convoyId}/messages/{id} {senderUid, text, createdAt, senderDisplayName, senderAvatarPath, mentionedUids} (denormalized sender profile; mentionedUids is always [] — this callable accepts no @mentions, the field exists so both chat channels share one message shape). Backend is the sole writer (firebase/firestore.rules grants reads only to accepted convoy members via a get() of the convoy doc, denies client writes). Returns { messageId }. Deployed via grouped export as convoyChat-post (functions/src/chatchannels/convoyChat.ts).

functions.name: convoyChat.list
functions.description: Paginated newest-first convoy chat messages ({ convoyId, before? } where before is an ISO-8601 createdAt cursor, exclusive). Only an accepted member of the convoy may read (same gate as convoyChat.post; missing convoy/outsider not-found, still-invited/declined failed-precondition). Returns { convoyId, messages:[{id,senderUid,text,senderDisplayName,senderAvatarPath,mentionedUids,createdAt}], nextBefore, hasMore } (page size 30). mentionedUids is always [] here — convoyChat.post accepts no @mentions (the chat already notifies every accepted member, so a mention notice would duplicate one they get anyway); the field is present only so both channels share one message shape. Deployed via grouped export as convoyChat-list (functions/src/chatchannels/convoyChat.ts).

functions.name: chatchannels.reportMessage
functions.description: Reports a message in either CHANNEL chat ({ channel: 'community'|'convoy', convoyId (required for and only for convoy), messageId, reason: harassment|hate_or_abuse|spam|unsafe_driving|privacy|other, details? <=500 chars }). One callable for both channels because only the eligibility check differs. Eligibility mirrors each channel's read rule: community = any active member; convoy = an ACCEPTED member of that convoy (same gate as convoyChat.post/list — missing convoy/outsider not-found, still-invited failed-precondition). Passing convoyId with channel 'community' (or omitting it for convoy) is invalid-argument, never silently ignored. Reporting your own message is invalid-argument. Ids are constrained to a single Firestore document-id segment (no `/`, no `.`/`..`, no reserved `__*__`) so a hostile id is invalid-argument rather than a traversal into another document. BLOCKING does NOT gate reporting either way. SNAPSHOTS the reported message (text + author uid/displayName + createdAt) because channel messages are TTL-deleted (community 120d / convoy 30d) and a report holding only ids would go blank. Deduplicates per channel+scope+message+reporter+reason (repeat silently refreshes details only; never resets a report a moderator already actioned). Rate-limited to 10 NEW reports/hour/reporter across all report types (resource-exhausted). Writes moderationReports/{reportId} (admin-read-only, client-write-denied). Returns { reported: true }. Deployed via grouped export as chatchannels-reportMessage (functions/src/chatchannels/reportMessage.ts).

functions.name: moderation.reportUser
functions.description: Reports a PERSON rather than a message ({ reportedUserId, reason: harassment|hate_or_abuse|spam|unsafe_driving|privacy|other, details? <=500 chars }) — the escalation for behaviour that doesn't reduce to one line of chat. AUTHENTICATED-active gate (requireActiveActor, matching blocking.block/unblock rather than the member-gated chat callables: reporting harassment must not require a live subscription; suspended/deleted still rejected). Self-report invalid-argument; a reportedUserId that is not a single Firestore document-id segment (no `/`, no `.`/`..`, no reserved `__*__`) is invalid-argument; missing or soft-deleted target not-found. BLOCKING does NOT gate reporting either way. Deduplicates per (reporter, reportedUser) WITHOUT the reason, so a single reporter cannot fill the queue by cycling the reason enum — a repeat updates reason+details and increments `occurrences` on the one document, which also makes the row count for a target equal the number of DISTINCT reporters. Captures ONLY the target's public profile projection (displayName+avatarPath, snapshotted so a rename doesn't orphan the row) plus the tally — never their message history, drives or garage. A per-target aggregate at moderationUserSummaries/{uid} ({reporterCount, totalSubmissions, lastReportedAt}) is maintained in the same transaction for O(1) 'how many prior reports' triage. Rate-limited to 10 NEW reports/hour/reporter across all report types (resource-exhausted). Writes moderationReports/{reportId} (admin-read-only, client-write-denied). Returns { reported: true }. Deployed via grouped export as moderation-reportUser (functions/src/moderation/reportUser.ts).

functions.name: incidents.report
functions.description: Creates a crowd-sourced road incident ({ type: accident|roadwork|hazard|police|road_closed, latitude, longitude, note? }, note <=200 chars). Member-gated. Writes incidents/{id} with a computed geoCell (coarse grid key used by listNearby instead of a full-collection scan), source:'user', reporterUid, a server createdAt, and a per-type expiresAt TTL (police 1h .. roadwork 12h). Clients cannot write the collection directly (firebase/firestore.rules denies all client writes), so a report cannot be forged, backdated, or spoofed as a Trafikverket import. Returns the IncidentView { id, type, latitude, longitude, source, reporterUid, note, createdAt, expiresAt, confirmationCount }. Deployed via grouped export as incidents-report (functions/src/incidents/report.ts).

functions.name: incidents.listNearby
functions.description: Bounded read of ACTIVE, unexpired incidents near a point ({ latitude, longitude, radiusMeters? }, radius clamped to 100..50000 m, default 15000). Open to ANY active signed-in user, not only members — the Waze-style map layer is shared by all users and this is a read. Enumerates the grid cells covering the radius and reads only those via chunked `geoCell in [...]` queries (+ status=='active' and expiresAt>now), then filters to the exact server-computed Haversine radius (a client-supplied distance is never trusted) and caps at 200. Returns { incidents: IncidentView[] }. Deployed via grouped export as incidents-listNearby (functions/src/incidents/listNearby.ts).

functions.name: incidents.remove
functions.description: Clears an incident the caller no longer stands behind ({ incidentId }). A signed-in caller may remove their OWN report; an admin may remove any (moderation). Idempotent: removing a missing incident is a no-op success ({ removed: false }). Imported (source!='user') incidents are failed-precondition for EVERYONE including admins — the Trafikverket sync would just re-upsert them. Deletes the document and its confirmations sub-collection (recursiveDelete) so the marker disappears for everyone on the next nearby fetch. Returns { removed }. Deployed via grouped export as incidents-remove (functions/src/incidents/remove.ts).

functions.name: incidents.confirm
functions.description: Confirms someone else's incident is still there ({ incidentId }) — the 'is this still there?' action on a marker. Declared access 'member' (requireMemberActor), matching incidents.report rather than the read-only listNearby: it is a write that keeps a marker alive for every user. NOTE the declared access is what is enforced WHEN THE GATE IS ON: functions/src/shared/memberGating.ts currently sets MEMBER_GATING_ENABLED = false repo-wide, so the entitlement half of every 'member' declaration in this registry is presently bypassed and any signed-in, non-suspended, non-deleted caller passes. Suspension and soft-deletion are NEVER bypassed. Re-locking is the documented five-switch procedure in memberGating.ts; this callable needs no change when it happens. ONE confirmation per user per incident, enforced by the document id of incidents/{id}/confirmations/{uid} claimed with tx.create in the same transaction that increments incidents/{id}.confirmationCount and extends expiresAt — concurrent double-taps cannot double-count. A repeat is idempotent success with alreadyConfirmed:true (no second write, no further extension), not an error. The reporter cannot confirm their own report (permission-denied). Confirming resets expiresAt to a fresh per-type TTL from now, never backwards and never past the hard cap createdAt + 3x the type's TTL, so a confirmed incident persists but can never become immortal. A missing incident is not-found; an inactive/expired one is failed-precondition; an imported (source!='user') one is failed-precondition because runTrafikverketSync full-overwrites each tv_ doc every 30 minutes and upstream is the authority on whether it is still live. No notification is sent to the reporter (ambient corroboration, not a social interaction). Returns { incidentId, confirmationCount, expiresAt, alreadyConfirmed }. Deployed via grouped export as incidents-confirm (functions/src/incidents/confirm.ts).
